newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. trade gap $8.4 bln in Nov.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. trade gap $8.4 bln in Nov.

text.p: Following are comments from economists after the Commerce Department reported the trade gap for November at $8.4 billion compared to a revised $8.01 billion in October.
U.S. economists in a Reuters survey expected a $9.8 billion deficit for the month.

ALAN RUSKIN, CHIEF ECONOMIST, I.D.E.A. INC: "Very, very impressive numbers indeed. The export numbers again held up rather well which does suggest that perhaps the October numbers were not quite as erratic as certainly I'd assumed."
"Aircraft exports did come off a little bit, perhaps not quite as much as I anticipated, but nonetheless the overall export picture is very very strong," Ruskin noted.

KEVIN FLANAGAN, VICE PRESIDENT AND ECONOMIST, DEAN WITTER REYNOLDS INC: "You did get some re-widening, but the overall reading itself was better than expected. This will probably mean trade will provide some support for GDP in the fourth quarter.

"The way the markets are focusing on it right now has more to do with its effects in the foreign exchange markets. It's pushed the dollar to its highs of the day, which is elevating Treasury prices at the same time."

Commenting on the 38.8 percent narrowing of the trade gap with China, Flanagan said: "That's just one month. It's been rising for the last two years on a monthly basis. I wouldn't read too much into that yet, it's just something you'd have to wait and reserve judgment on."

CHARLES LIEBERMAN, MANAGING DIRECTOR AND DIRECTOR OF FINANCIAL MARKETS RESEARCH, CHASE SECURITIES INC: "It was substantially better than expected. There was only a slight deterioration in November after the enormous improvement in the trade account in October. Oil imports fell. On the export side, aircraft shipments didn't fall as much as expected. Total exports were actually up a little bit instead of declining.

"It's going to cause us to revise upward our GDP estimate. Our last estimate was 3.2 percent. We'll end up with an estimate of 3.5 percent to 4.0 percent, quite possibly in the upper end of that range."

EVELINA TAINER, CHIEF ECONOMIST, INDOSUEZ CARR FUTURES: "This is definitely good news for the dollar. It means a lot more strength in fourth-quarter GDP (Gross Domestic Product). We could easily start talking about GDP coming in over 4.0 percent. So that's not going to be good for the bond market."

ASTRID ADOLFSON, FIRST VICE PRESIDENT AND ECONOMIST, MCM MONEYWATCH INC: "It shows that the trade deficit remained low, and if anything, that suggests that the fourth-quarter GDP could be the 4.0 to 4.0-plus percent given all the other variables that are in place -- namely the inventories didn't subtract enough and consumer spending and other factors are continuing to add to GDP."
"The gap, interestingly enough, between Japan and China narrowed ... It does show that we are doing a little bit better on the export side."
